metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the LORD’s word came to the prophet Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying,
units.rightText: In the eighth month of the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying:
leftNotes: 1:1 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: “The LORD was very displeased with your fathers.
units.rightText: “The LORD was very angry with your fathers.

units.leftText: Therefore tell them, the LORD of Armies says: ‘Return to me,’ says the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will return to you,’ says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: So tell the people that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of Hosts.’

units.leftText: Don’t you be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying: The LORD of Armies says, ‘Return now from your evil ways and from your evil doings;’ but they didn’t hear nor listen to me, says the LORD.
units.rightText: Do not be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Turn now from your evil ways and deeds.’

units.leftText: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?
units.rightText: Where are your fathers now? And the prophets, do they live forever?

units.leftText: But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, didn’t they overtake your fathers?
units.rightText: But did not My words and My statutes, which I commanded My servants the prophets, overtake your fathers? They repented and said, ‘Just as the LORD of Hosts purposed to do to us according to our ways and deeds, so He has done to us.’”

units.leftText: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the LORD’s word came to the prophet Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying,
units.rightText: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to the prophet Zechariah son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo.
rightNotes: 1:7 Shebat is the eleventh month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of January and February.

units.leftText: “I had a vision in the night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine; and behind him there were red, brown, and white horses.
units.rightText: I looked out into the night and saw a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in the hollow, and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
leftNotes: 1:8 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: Then I asked, ‘My lord, what are these?’”
units.rightText: “What are these, my lord?” I asked.

units.leftText: The man who stood among the myrtle trees answered, “They are the ones the LORD has sent to go back and forth through the earth.”
units.rightText: Then the man standing among the myrtle trees explained, “They are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”

units.leftText: They reported to the LORD’s angel who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, “We have walked back and forth through the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and in peace.”
units.rightText: And the riders answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees, “We have patrolled the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and tranquil.”

units.leftText: Then the LORD’s angel replied, “O LORD of Armies, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which you have had indignation these seventy years?”
units.rightText: Then the angel of the LORD said, “How long, O LORD of Hosts, will You withhold mercy from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which You have been angry these seventy years?”

units.leftText: The LORD answered the angel who talked with me with kind and comforting words.
units.rightText: So the LORD spoke kind and comforting words to the angel who was speaking with me.

units.leftText: So the angel who talked with me said to me, “Proclaim, saying, ‘The LORD of Armies says: “I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.
units.rightText: Then the angel who was speaking with me said, “Proclaim this word: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘I am very jealous for Jerusalem and Zion,

units.leftText: I am very angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was but a little displeased, but they added to the calamity.”
units.rightText: but I am fiercely angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was a little angry, but they have added to the calamity. ’
rightNotes: 1:15 Or they have overdone the punishment

units.leftText: Therefore the LORD says: “I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy. My house shall be built in it,” says the LORD of Armies, “and a line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.”’
units.rightText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘I will return to Jerusalem with mercy, and there My house will be rebuilt, declares the LORD of Hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.’

units.leftText: “Proclaim further, saying, ‘The LORD of Armies says: “My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and the LORD will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem.”’”
units.rightText: Proclaim further that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘My cities will again overflow with prosperity; the LORD will again comfort Zion and choose Jerusalem.’”

units.leftText: I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, four horns.
units.rightText: Then I looked up and saw four horns.

units.leftText: I asked the angel who talked with me, “What are these?”
units.rightText: So I asked the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these?”

units.leftText: The LORD showed me four craftsmen.
units.rightText: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

units.leftText: Then I asked, “What are these coming to do?”
units.rightText: “What are these coming to do?” I asked.

units.leftText: I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, a man with a measuring line in his hand.
units.rightText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.

units.leftText: Then I asked, “Where are you going?”
units.rightText: “Where are you going?” I asked.

units.leftText: Behold, the angel who talked with me went out, and another angel went out to meet him,
units.rightText: Then the angel who was speaking with me went forth, and another angel came forward to meet him

units.leftText: and said to him, “Run, speak to this young man, saying, ‘Jerusalem will be inhabited as villages without walls, because of the multitude of men and livestock in it.
units.rightText: and said to him, “Run and tell that young man: ‘Jerusalem will be a city without walls because of the multitude of men and livestock within it.

units.leftText: For I,’ says the LORD, ‘will be to her a wall of fire around it, and I will be the glory in the middle of her.
units.rightText: For I will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within it.’”

units.leftText: Come! Come! Flee from the land of the north,’ says the LORD; ‘for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the sky,’ says the LORD.
units.rightText: “Get up! Get up! Flee from the land of the north,” declares the LORD, “for I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: ‘Come, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.’
units.rightText: “Get up, O Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the Daughter of Babylon!”

units.leftText: For the LORD of Armies says: ‘For honor he has sent me to the nations which plundered you; for he who touches you touches the apple of his eye.
units.rightText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “After His Glory has sent Me against the nations that have plundered you — for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye —
rightNotes: 2:8 Or After the Glorious One has sent Me or After He has honored Me and sent Me
2:8 Or the pupil

units.leftText: For, behold, I will shake my hand over them, and they will be a plunder to those who served them; and you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me.
units.rightText: I will surely wave My hand over them, so that they will become plunder for their own servants. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me.”

units.leftText: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion! For behold, I come and I will dwell within you,’ says the LORD.
units.rightText: “Shout for joy and be glad, O Daughter of Zion, for I am coming to dwell among you,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: Many nations shall join themselves to the LORD in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell among you, and you shall know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
units.rightText: “On that day many nations will join themselves to the LORD, and they will become My people. I will dwell among you, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you.

units.leftText: The LORD will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And the LORD will take possession of Judah as His portion in the Holy Land, and He will once again choose Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD; for he has roused himself from his holy habitation!”
units.rightText: Be silent before the LORD, all people, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.”

units.leftText: He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the LORD’s angel, and Satan standing at his right hand to be his adversary.
units.rightText: Then the angel showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
rightNotes: 3:1 Or Angel; also in verses 3, 4, 5, and 6; corresponding pronouns may also be capitalized.
3:1 That is, the Accuser or the Adversary; also in verse 2

units.leftText: The LORD said to Satan, “The LORD rebuke you, Satan! Yes, the LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”
units.rightText: And the LORD said to Satan: “The LORD rebukes you, Satan! Indeed, the LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebukes you! Is not this man a firebrand snatched from the fire?”
rightNotes: 3:2 That is, a burning stick

units.leftText: Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and was standing before the angel.
units.rightText: Now Joshua was dressed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.

units.leftText: He answered and spoke to those who stood before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he said, “Behold, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”
units.rightText: So the angel said to those standing before him, “Take off his filthy clothes!”

units.leftText: I said, “Let them set a clean turban on his head.”
units.rightText: Then I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So a clean turban was placed on his head, and they clothed him, as the angel of the LORD stood by.

units.leftText: The LORD’s angel solemnly assured Joshua, saying,
units.rightText: Then the angel of the LORD gave this charge to Joshua:

units.leftText: “The LORD of Armies says: ‘If you will walk in my ways, and if you will follow my instructions, then you also shall judge my house, and shall also keep my courts, and I will give you a place of access among these who stand by.
units.rightText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘If you walk in My ways and keep My instructions, then you will govern My house and will also have charge of My courts; and I will give you a place among these who are standing here.

units.leftText: Hear now, Joshua the high priest, you and your fellows who sit before you, for they are men who are a sign; for, behold, I will bring out my servant, the Branch.
units.rightText: Hear now, O high priest Joshua, you and your companions seated before you, who are indeed a sign. For behold, I am going to bring My servant, the Branch.

units.leftText: For, behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua: on one stone are seven eyes; behold, I will engrave its inscription,’ says the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day.
units.rightText: See the stone I have set before Joshua; on that one stone are seven eyes. Behold, I will engrave on it an inscription, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the iniquity of this land in a single day.
rightNotes: 3:9 Or facets

units.leftText: In that day,’ says the LORD of Armies, ‘you will invite every man his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.’”
units.rightText: On that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, you will each invite your neighbor to sit under your own vine and fig tree.’”

units.leftText: The angel who talked with me came again and wakened me, as a man who is wakened out of his sleep.
units.rightText: Then the angel who was speaking with me returned and woke me, as a man is awakened from his sleep.

units.leftText: He said to me, “What do you see?”
units.rightText: “What do you see?” he asked.

units.leftText: and two olive trees by it, one on the right side of the bowl, and the other on the left side of it.”
units.rightText: There are also two olive trees beside it, one on the right side of the bowl and the other on its left.”

units.leftText: I answered and spoke to the angel who talked with me, saying, “What are these, my lord?”
units.rightText: “What are these, my lord?” I asked the angel who was speaking with me.

units.leftText: Then the angel who talked with me answered me, “Don’t you know what these are?”
units.rightText: “Do you not know what they are?” replied the angel.

units.leftText: Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, “This is the LORD’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: So he said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you are a plain; and he will bring out the capstone with shouts of ‘Grace, grace, to it!’”
units.rightText: What are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. Then he will bring forth the capstone accompanied by shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’”

units.leftText: Moreover the LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house. His hands shall also finish it; and you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
units.rightText: “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.

units.leftText: Indeed, who despises the day of small things? For these seven shall rejoice, and shall see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These are the LORD’s eyes, which run back and forth through the whole earth.”
units.rightText: For who has despised the day of small things? But these seven eyes of the LORD, which scan the whole earth, will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel.”
rightNotes: 4:10 Or facets
4:10 Or the chosen capstone

units.leftText: Then I asked him, “What are these two olive trees on the right side of the lamp stand and on the left side of it?”
units.rightText: Then I asked the angel, “What are the two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”

units.leftText: I asked him the second time, “What are these two olive branches, which are beside the two golden spouts that pour the golden oil out of themselves?”
units.rightText: And I questioned him further, “What are the two olive branches beside the two gold pipes from which the golden oil pours?”
rightNotes: 4:12 Hebrew from which the gold

units.leftText: He answered me, “Don’t you know what these are?”
units.rightText: “Do you not know what these are?” he inquired.

units.leftText: Then he said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”
units.rightText: So he said, “These are the two anointed ones who are standing beside the Lord of all the earth.”
rightNotes: 4:14 Hebrew the two sons of new oil
4:14 See Revelation 11:4|REV 11:4*.

units.leftText: Then again I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, a flying scroll.
units.rightText: Again I lifted up my eyes and saw before me a flying scroll.

units.leftText: He said to me, “What do you see?”
units.rightText: “What do you see?” asked the angel.

units.leftText: Then he said to me, “This is the curse that goes out over the surface of the whole land, for everyone who steals shall be cut off according to it on the one side; and everyone who swears falsely shall be cut off according to it on the other side.
units.rightText: Then he told me, “This is the curse that is going out over the face of all the land, for according to one side of the scroll, every thief will be removed; and according to the other side, every perjurer will be removed.

units.leftText: I will cause it to go out,” says the LORD of Armies, “and it will enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him who swears falsely by my name; and it will remain in the middle of his house, and will destroy it with its timber and its stones.”
units.rightText: I will send it out, declares the LORD of Hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of him who swears falsely by My name. It will remain inside his house and destroy it, down to its timbers and stones.”

units.leftText: Then the angel who talked with me came forward and said to me, “Lift up now your eyes and see what this is that is appearing.”
units.rightText: Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and told me, “Now lift up your eyes and see what is approaching.”

units.leftText: I said, “What is it?”
units.rightText: “What is it?” I asked.

units.leftText: and behold, a lead cover weighing one talent was lifted up—and there was a woman sitting in the middle of the ephah basket.”
units.rightText: And behold, the cover of lead was raised, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
leftNotes: 5:7 A talent is about 30 kilograms or 66 pounds.
5:7 1 ephah is about 22 liters or about 2/3 of a bushel

units.leftText: He said, “This is Wickedness;” and he threw her down into the middle of the ephah basket; and he threw the lead weight on its mouth.
units.rightText: “This is Wickedness,” he said. And he shoved her down into the basket, pushing down the lead cover over its opening.

units.leftText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, there were two women; and the wind was in their wings. Now they had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the ephah basket between earth and the sky.
units.rightText: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw two women approaching, with the wind in their wings. Their wings were like those of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between heaven and earth.

units.leftText: Then I said to the angel who talked with me, “Where are these carrying the ephah basket?”
units.rightText: “Where are they taking the basket?” I asked the angel who was speaking with me.

units.leftText: He said to me, “To build her a house in the land of Shinar. When it is prepared, she will be set there in her own place.”
units.rightText: “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar, ” he told me. “And when it is ready, the basket will be set there on its pedestal.”
rightNotes: 5:11 That is, Babylonia

units.leftText: Again I lifted up my eyes, and saw, and behold, four chariots came out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
units.rightText: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains — mountains of bronze.

units.leftText: In the first chariot were red horses. In the second chariot were black horses.
units.rightText: The first chariot had red horses, the second black horses,

units.leftText: In the third chariot were white horses. In the fourth chariot were dappled horses, all of them powerful.
units.rightText: the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses— all of them strong.

units.leftText: Then I asked the angel who talked with me, “What are these, my lord?”
units.rightText: So I inquired of the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”

units.leftText: The angel answered me, “These are the four winds of the sky, which go out from standing before the Lord of all the earth.
units.rightText: And the angel told me, “These are the four spirits of heaven, going forth from their station before the Lord of all the earth.
rightNotes: 6:5 Or winds

units.leftText: The one with the black horses goes out toward the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out toward the south country.”
units.rightText: The one with the black horses is going toward the land of the north, the one with the white horses toward the west, and the one with the dappled horses toward the south.”
rightNotes: 6:6 Or the one with the white horses after them

units.leftText: The strong went out, and sought to go that they might walk back and forth through the earth. He said, “Go around and through the earth!” So they walked back and forth through the earth.
units.rightText: As the strong horses went out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth; and the LORD said, “Go and patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.

units.leftText: Then he called to me, and spoke to me, saying, “Behold, those who go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.”
units.rightText: Then the LORD summoned me and said, “Behold, those going to the land of the north have given rest to My Spirit in the land of the north.”

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to me, saying,
units.rightText: The word of the LORD also came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah; and come the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, where they have come from Babylon.
units.rightText: “Take an offering from the exiles — from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon — and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

units.leftText: Yes, take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest;
units.rightText: Take silver and gold, make an ornate crown, and set it on the head of the high priest, Joshua son of Jehozadak.
rightNotes: 6:11 Jehozadak is a variant of Jozadak; see Ezra 3:2|EZR 3:2*.

units.leftText: and speak to him, saying, ‘The LORD of Armies says, “Behold, the man whose name is the Branch! He will grow up out of his place; and he will build the LORD’s temple.
units.rightText: And you are to tell him that this is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Here is a man whose name is the Branch, and He will branch out from His place and build the temple of the LORD.

units.leftText: He will build the LORD’s temple. He will bear the glory, and will sit and rule on his throne. He will be a priest on his throne. The counsel of peace will be between them both.
units.rightText: Yes, He will build the temple of the LORD; He will be clothed in splendor and will sit on His throne and rule. And He will be a priest on His throne, and there will be peaceful counsel between the two.’
rightNotes: 6:13 Or And there will be a priest on His throne

units.leftText: The crowns shall be to Helem, to Tobijah, to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the LORD’s temple.
units.rightText: The crown will reside in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and the gracious son of Zephaniah.
rightNotes: 6:14 Hebrew; Syriac Heldai; see verse 10.
6:14 Or and Hen; Syriac and Josiah; see verse 10.

units.leftText: Those who are far off shall come and build in the LORD’s temple; and you shall know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you. This will happen, if you will diligently obey the LORD your God’s voice.”’”
units.rightText: Even those far away will come and build the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me to you. This will happen if you diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God.”

units.leftText: In the fourth year of King Darius, the LORD’s word came to Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev.
units.rightText: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev.
rightNotes: 7:1 Chislev is the ninth month of the Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of November and December.

units.leftText: The people of Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem Melech and their men to entreat the LORD’s favor,
units.rightText: Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech, along with their men, to plead before the LORD
rightNotes: 7:2 Or Bethel-sharezer had sent Regem-melech, along with his men,

units.leftText: and to speak to the priests of the house of the LORD of Armies and to the prophets, saying, “Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?”
units.rightText: by asking the priests of the house of the LORD of Hosts, as well as the prophets, “Should I weep and fast in the fifth month, as I have done these many years?”

units.leftText: Then the word of the LORD of Armies came to me, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying,

units.leftText: “Speak to all the people of the land and to the priests, saying, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month for these seventy years, did you at all fast to me, really to me?
units.rightText: “Ask all the people of the land and the priests, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for these seventy years, was it really for Me that you fasted?

units.leftText: When you eat and when you drink, don’t you eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves?
units.rightText: And when you were eating and drinking, were you not doing so simply for yourselves?

units.leftText: Aren’t these the words which the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and its cities around her, and the South and the lowland were inhabited?’”
units.rightText: Are these not the words that the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were populous and prosperous, and the Negev and the foothills were inhabited?’”
rightNotes: 7:7 Hebrew Shephelah or lowlands; that is, the western foothills of Judea

units.leftText: The LORD’s word came to Zechariah, saying,
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah, saying,

units.leftText: “Thus has the LORD of Armies spoken, saying, ‘Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother.
units.rightText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: ‘Administer true justice. Show loving devotion and compassion to one another.
rightNotes: 7:9 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: Don’t oppress the widow, the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.’
units.rightText: Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor. And do not plot evil in your hearts against one another.’

units.leftText: But they refused to listen, and turned their backs, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear.
units.rightText: But they refused to pay attention and turned a stubborn shoulder; they stopped up their ears from hearing.
rightNotes: 7:11 Hebrew they made their ears too heavy to hear

units.leftText: Yes, they made their hearts as hard as flint, lest they might hear the law and the words which the LORD of Armies had sent by his Spirit by the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: They made their hearts like flint and would not listen to the law or to the words that the LORD of Hosts had sent by His Spirit through the earlier prophets. Therefore great anger came from the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: It has come to pass that, as he called and they refused to listen, so they will call and I will not listen,” said the LORD of Armies;
units.rightText: And just as I had called and they would not listen, so when they called I would not listen, says the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: “but I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they have not known. Thus the land was desolate after them, so that no man passed through nor returned; for they made the pleasant land desolate.”
units.rightText: But I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations that they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them so that no one could come or go. Thus they turned the pleasant land into a desolation.”

units.leftText: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me.
units.rightText: Again the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying:

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.”
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor.”

units.leftText: The LORD says: “I have returned to Zion, and will dwell in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called ‘The City of Truth;’ and the mountain of the LORD of Armies, ‘The Holy Mountain.’”
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “I will return to Zion and dwell in Jerusalem. Then Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts will be called the Holy Mountain.”

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “Old men and old women will again dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, every man with his staff in his hand because of their old age.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Old men and old women will again sit along the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.

units.leftText: The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.”
units.rightText: And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing there.”

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “If it is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be marvelous in my eyes?” says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in My eyes?” declares the LORD of Hosts.
rightNotes: 8:6 Or marvelous; twice in this verse

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “Behold, I will save my people from the east country and from the west country.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.

units.leftText: I will bring them, and they will dwell within Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”
units.rightText: I will bring them back to dwell in Jerusalem, where they will be My people, and I will be their faithful and righteous God.”

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets who were in the day that the foundation of the house of the LORD of Armies was laid, even the temple, that it might be built.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words spoken by the prophets who were present when the foundations were laid to rebuild the temple, the house of the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: For before those days there was no wages for man nor any wages for an animal, neither was there any peace to him who went out or came in, because of the adversary. For I set all men everyone against his neighbor.
units.rightText: For before those days neither man nor beast received wages, nor was there safety from the enemy for anyone who came or went, for I had turned every man against his neighbor.

units.leftText: But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days,” says the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as I did in the past,” declares the LORD of Hosts.

units.leftText: “For the seed of peace and the vine will yield its fruit, and the ground will give its increase, and the heavens will give their dew. I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.
units.rightText: “For the seed will be prosperous, the vine will yield its fruit, the ground will yield its produce, and the skies will give their dew. To the remnant of this people I will give all these things as an inheritance.

units.leftText: It shall come to pass that, as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall be a blessing. Don’t be afraid. Let your hands be strong.”
units.rightText: As you have been a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”

units.leftText: For the LORD of Armies says: “As I thought to do evil to you when your fathers provoked me to wrath,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I didn’t repent,
units.rightText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Just as I resolved to bring disaster upon you when your fathers provoked Me to anger, and I did not relent,” says the LORD of Hosts,

units.leftText: so again I have thought in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Don’t be afraid.
units.rightText: “so now I have resolved to do good again to Jerusalem and Judah. Do not be afraid.

units.leftText: These are the things that you shall do: speak every man the truth with his neighbor. Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates,
units.rightText: These are the things you must do: Speak truth to one another, render true and sound judgments in your gates,

units.leftText: and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor, and love no false oath; for all these are things that I hate,” says the LORD.
units.rightText: do not plot evil in your hearts against your neighbor, and do not love to swear falsely, for I hate all these things,” declares the LORD.

units.leftText: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me.
units.rightText: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me, saying,

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months shall be for the house of Judah joy, gladness, and cheerful feasts. Therefore love truth and peace.”
units.rightText: “This is what the LORD of Hosts says: The fasts of the fourth, the fifth, the seventh, and the tenth months will become times of joy and gladness, cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Therefore you are to love both truth and peace.”

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “Many peoples and the inhabitants of many cities will yet come.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Peoples will yet come — the residents of many cities —

units.leftText: The inhabitants of one will go to another, saying, ‘Let’s go speedily to entreat the favor of the LORD, and to seek the LORD of Armies. I will go also.’
units.rightText: and the residents of one city will go to another, saying: ‘Let us go at once to plead before the LORD and to seek the LORD of Hosts. I myself am going.’

units.leftText: Yes, many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to entreat the favor of the LORD.”
units.rightText: And many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the LORD.”

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies says: “In those days, ten men out of all the languages of the nations will take hold of the skirt of him who is a Jew, saying, ‘We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”
units.rightText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “In those days ten men from the nations of every tongue will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew, saying, ‘Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”

units.leftText: A revelation.
units.rightText: This is the burden of the word of the LORD

units.leftText: and Hamath, also, which borders on it,
units.rightText: and also against Hamath,

units.leftText: Tyre built herself a stronghold,
units.rightText: Tyre has built herself a fortress;

units.leftText: Behold, the Lord will dispossess her,
units.rightText: Behold, the Lord will impoverish her

units.leftText: Ashkelon will see it, and fear;
units.rightText: Ashkelon will see and fear;

units.leftText: Foreigners will dwell in Ashdod,
units.rightText: A mixed race will occupy Ashdod,

units.leftText: I will take away his blood out of his mouth,
units.rightText: I will remove the blood from their mouths

units.leftText: I will encamp around my house against the army,
units.rightText: But I will camp around My house because of an army,

units.leftText: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion!
units.rightText: Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion!

units.leftText: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim
units.rightText: And I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim
rightNotes: 9:10 That is, the northern kingdom of Israel

units.leftText: As for you also,
units.rightText: As for you,

units.leftText: Turn to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope!
units.rightText: Return to your stronghold,

units.leftText: For indeed I bend Judah as a bow for me.
units.rightText: For I will bend Judah as My bow

units.leftText: The LORD will be seen over them.
units.rightText: Then the LORD will appear over them,

units.leftText: The LORD of Armies will defend them.
units.rightText: The LORD of Hosts will shield them.

units.leftText: The LORD their God will save them in that day as the flock of his people;
units.rightText: On that day the LORD their God will save them

units.leftText: For how great is his goodness,
units.rightText: How lovely they will be,

units.leftText: Ask of the LORD rain in the spring time,
units.rightText: Ask the LORD for rain in springtime;

units.leftText: For the teraphim have spoken vanity,
units.rightText: For idols speak deceit
leftNotes: 10:2 teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property.

units.leftText: My anger is kindled against the shepherds,
units.rightText: “My anger burns against the shepherds,

units.leftText: From him will come the cornerstone,
units.rightText: The cornerstone will come from Judah,

units.leftText: They will be as mighty men,
units.rightText: They will be like mighty men in battle,

units.leftText: “I will strengthen the house of Judah,
units.rightText: I will strengthen the house of Judah

units.leftText: Ephraim will be like a mighty man,
units.rightText: Ephraim will be like a mighty man,

units.leftText: I will signal for them and gather them,
units.rightText: I will whistle for them to gather,

units.leftText: I will sow them among the peoples.
units.rightText: Though I sow them among the nations,

units.leftText: I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt,
units.rightText: I will bring them back from Egypt

units.leftText: He will pass through the sea of affliction,
units.rightText: They will pass through the sea of distress

units.leftText: I will strengthen them in the LORD.
units.rightText: I will strengthen them in the LORD,

units.leftText: Open your doors, Lebanon,
units.rightText: Open your doors, O Lebanon,

units.leftText: Wail, cypress tree, for the cedar has fallen,
units.rightText: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen;
rightNotes: 11:2 Or pine or juniper or fir

units.leftText: A voice of the wailing of the shepherds!
units.rightText: Listen to the wailing of the shepherds,

units.leftText: The LORD my God says: “Feed the flock of slaughter.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD my God says: “Pasture the flock marked for slaughter,

units.leftText: Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich;’ and their own shepherds don’t pity them.
units.rightText: whose buyers slaughter them without remorse. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich!’ Even their own shepherds have no compassion on them.

units.leftText: For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land,” says the LORD; “but, behold, I will deliver every one of the men into his neighbor’s hand and into the hand of his king. They will strike the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.”
units.rightText: For I will no longer have compassion on the people of the land, declares the LORD, but behold, I will cause each man to fall into the hands of his neighbor and his king, who will devastate the land, and I will not deliver it from their hands.”

units.leftText: So I fed the flock to be slaughtered, especially the oppressed of the flock. I took for myself two staffs. The one I called “Favor” and the other I called “Union”, and I fed the flock.
units.rightText: So I pastured the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. Then I took for myself two staffs, calling one Favor and the other Union, and I pastured the flock.

units.leftText: I cut off the three shepherds in one month; for my soul was weary of them, and their soul also loathed me.
units.rightText: And in one month I dismissed three shepherds.

units.leftText: Then I said, “I will not feed you. That which dies, let it die; and that which is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let those who are left eat each other’s flesh.”
units.rightText: Then I said, “I will no longer shepherd you. Let the dying die, and the perishing perish; and let those who remain devour one another’s flesh.”

units.leftText: I took my staff Favor and cut it apart, that I might break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
units.rightText: Next I took my staff called Favor and cut it in two, revoking the covenant I had made with all the nations.
rightNotes: 11:10 Or broke it; similarly in verse 14

units.leftText: It was broken in that day; and thus the poor of the flock that listened to me knew that it was the LORD’s word.
units.rightText: It was revoked on that day, and so the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.

units.leftText: I said to them, “If you think it best, give me my wages; and if not, keep them.” So they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver.
units.rightText: Then I told them, “If it seems right to you, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.” So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.

units.leftText: The LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—the handsome price that I was valued at by them!” I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the LORD’s house.
units.rightText: And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”— this magnificent price at which they valued me. So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.

units.leftText: Then I cut apart my other staff, Union, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
units.rightText: Then I cut in two my second staff called Union, breaking the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

units.leftText: The LORD said to me, “Take for yourself yet again the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
units.rightText: And the LORD said to me: “Take up once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

units.leftText: For, behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will not visit those who are cut off, neither will seek those who are scattered, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which is sound; but he will eat the meat of the fat sheep, and will tear their hoofs in pieces.
units.rightText: For behold, I will raise up a shepherd in the land who will neither care for the lost, nor seek the young, nor heal the broken, nor sustain the healthy, but he will devour the flesh of the choice sheep and tear off their hooves.

units.leftText: Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! The sword will strike his arm and his right eye. His arm will be completely withered, and his right eye will be totally blinded!”
units.rightText: Woe to the worthless shepherd,

units.leftText: A revelation of the LORD’s word concerning Israel: The LORD, who stretches out the heavens and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him says:
units.rightText: This is the burden of the word of the LORD concerning Israel.

units.leftText: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling to all the surrounding peoples, and it will also be on Judah in the siege against Jerusalem.
units.rightText: “Behold, I will make Jerusalem a cup of drunkenness to all the surrounding peoples. Judah will be besieged, as well as Jerusalem.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples. All who burden themselves with it will be severely wounded, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against it.
units.rightText: On that day, when all the nations of the earth gather against her, I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples; all who would heave it away will be severely injured.

units.leftText: In that day,” says the LORD, “I will strike every horse with terror and his rider with madness. I will open my eyes on the house of Judah, and will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
units.rightText: On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic, and every rider with madness. I will keep a watchful eye on the house of Judah, but I will strike with blindness all the horses of the nations.

units.leftText: The chieftains of Judah will say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength in the LORD of Armies their God.’
units.rightText: Then the leaders of Judah will say in their hearts: ‘The people of Jerusalem are my strength, for the LORD of Hosts is their God.’

units.leftText: In that day I will make the chieftains of Judah like a pan of fire among wood, and like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will devour all the surrounding peoples on the right hand and on the left; and Jerusalem will yet again dwell in their own place, even in Jerusalem.
units.rightText: On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a firepot in a woodpile, like a flaming torch among the sheaves; they will consume all the peoples around them on the right and on the left, while the people of Jerusalem remain secure there.

units.leftText: The LORD also will save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of David’s house and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem not be magnified above Judah.
units.rightText: The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and of the people of Jerusalem may not be greater than that of Judah.

units.leftText: In that day the LORD will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He who is feeble among them at that day will be like David, and David’s house will be like God, like the LORD’s angel before them.
units.rightText: On that day the LORD will defend the people of Jerusalem, so that the weakest among them will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.
rightNotes: 12:8 Or Angel

units.leftText: It will happen in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
units.rightText: So on that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

units.leftText: I will pour on David’s house and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem the spirit of grace and of supplication. They will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him as one mourns for his only son, and will grieve bitterly for him as one grieves for his firstborn.
units.rightText: Then I will pour out on the house of David and on the people of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and prayer, and they will look on Me, the One they have pierced. They will mourn for Him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for Him as one grieves for a firstborn son.
leftNotes: 12:10 After “me”, the Hebrew has the two letters “Aleph Tav” (the first and last letters of the Hebrew alphabet), not as a word, but as a grammatical marker.
rightNotes: 12:10 Or the Spirit
12:10 Or to Me
12:10 Cited in John 19:37|JHN 19:37*

units.leftText: In that day there will be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo.
units.rightText: On that day the wailing in Jerusalem will be as great as the wailing of Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.

units.leftText: The land will mourn, every family apart; the family of David’s house apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
units.rightText: The land will mourn, each clan on its own: the clan of the house of David and their wives, the clan of the house of Nathan and their wives,

units.leftText: the family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;
units.rightText: the clan of the house of Levi and their wives, the clan of Shimei and their wives,

units.leftText: all the families who remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.
units.rightText: and all the remaining clans and their wives.[’’]

units.leftText: “In that day there will be a fountain opened to David’s house and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for uncleanness.
units.rightText: “On that day a fountain will be opened to the house of David and the people of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.

units.leftText: It will come to pass in that day, says the LORD of Armies, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also cause the prophets and the spirit of impurity to pass out of the land.
units.rightText: And on that day, declares the LORD of Hosts, I will erase the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
rightNotes: 13:2 Or the unclean spirit

units.leftText: It will happen that when anyone still prophesies, then his father and his mother who bore him will tell him, ‘You must die, because you speak lies in the LORD’s name;’ and his father and his mother who bore him will stab him when he prophesies.
units.rightText: And if anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, ‘You shall not remain alive, because you have spoken falsely in the name of the LORD.’ When he prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will pierce him through.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that the prophets will each be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies; they won’t wear a hairy mantle to deceive,
units.rightText: And on that day every prophet who prophesies will be ashamed of his vision, and he will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.

units.leftText: but he will say, ‘I am no prophet, I am a tiller of the ground; for I have been made a bondservant from my youth.’
units.rightText: He will say, ‘I am not a prophet; I work the land, for I was purchased as a servant in my youth. ’
rightNotes: 13:5 Or I am a farmer, for the land has been my livelihood since my youth.

units.leftText: One will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?’ Then he will answer, ‘Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.’
units.rightText: If someone asks him, ‘What are these wounds on your chest ?’ he will answer, ‘These are the wounds I received in the house of my friends.’
rightNotes: 13:6 Literally between your hands

units.leftText: “Awake, sword, against my shepherd,
units.rightText: Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd,

units.leftText: It shall happen that in all the land,” says the LORD,
units.rightText: And in all the land,

units.leftText: I will bring the third part into the fire,
units.rightText: This third I will bring through the fire;

units.leftText: Behold, a day of the LORD comes, when your plunder will be divided within you.
units.rightText: Behold, a day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided in your presence.

units.leftText: For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city will be taken, the houses rifled, and the women ravished. Half of the city will go out into captivity, and the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
units.rightText: For I will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem, and the city will be captured, the houses looted, and the women ravished. Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be removed from the city.

units.leftText: Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as when he fought in the day of battle.
units.rightText: Then the LORD will go out to fight against those nations, as He fights in the day of battle.

units.leftText: His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west, making a very great valley. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
units.rightText: On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west, forming a great valley, with half the mountain moving to the north and half to the south.

units.leftText: You shall flee by the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains shall reach to Azel. Yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. The LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with you.
units.rightText: You will flee by My mountain valley, for it will extend to Azal. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with Him.
rightNotes: 14:5 LXX; Hebrew with You

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that there will not be light, cold, or frost.
units.rightText: On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost.

units.leftText: It will be a unique day which is known to the LORD—not day, and not night; but it will come to pass that at evening time there will be light.
units.rightText: It will be a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night; but when evening comes, there will be light.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that living waters will go out from Jerusalem, half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea. It will be so in summer and in winter.
units.rightText: And on that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it toward the Eastern Sea and the other half toward the Western Sea, in summer and winter alike.
rightNotes: 14:8 That is, the Dead Sea
14:8 That is, the Mediterranean Sea, also called the Great Sea

units.leftText: The LORD will be King over all the earth. In that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.
units.rightText: On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth— the LORD alone, and His name alone.

units.leftText: All the land will be made like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she will be lifted up and will dwell in her place, from Benjamin’s gate to the place of the first gate, to the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananel to the king’s wine presses.
units.rightText: All the land from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem will be turned into a plain, but Jerusalem will be raised up and will remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the royal winepresses.

units.leftText: Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely.
units.rightText: People will live there, and never again will there be an utter destruction. So Jerusalem will dwell securely.

units.leftText: This will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who have fought against Jerusalem: their flesh will consume away while they stand on their feet, and their eyes will consume away in their sockets, and their tongue will consume away in their mouth.
units.rightText: And this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes all the peoples who have warred against Jerusalem: Their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.

units.leftText: It will happen in that day that a great panic from the LORD will be among them; and they will each seize the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will rise up against the hand of his neighbor.
units.rightText: On that day a great panic from the LORD will come upon them, so that each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will rise against the other.

units.leftText: Judah also will fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered together: gold, silver, and clothing, in great abundance.
units.rightText: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be collected — gold, silver, and apparel in great abundance.

units.leftText: A plague like this will fall on the horse, on the mule, on the camel, on the donkey, and on all the animals that will be in those camps.
units.rightText: And a similar plague will strike the horses and mules, camels and donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.

units.leftText: It will happen that everyone who is left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, and to keep the feast of booths.
units.rightText: Then all the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.
rightNotes: 14:16 That is, Sukkot, the autumn feast of pilgrimage to Jerusalem; also translated as the Feast of Booths or the Feast of Shelters and originally called the Feast of Ingathering(see Exodus 23:16|EXO 23:16* and Exodus 34:22).

units.leftText: It will be that whoever of all the families of the earth doesn’t go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, on them there will be no rain.
units.rightText: And should any of the families of the earth not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, then the rain will not fall on them.

units.leftText: If the family of Egypt doesn’t go up and doesn’t come, neither will it rain on them. This will be the plague with which the LORD will strike the nations that don’t go up to keep the feast of booths.
units.rightText: And if the people of Egypt will not go up and enter in, then the rain will not fall on them; this will be the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations who do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

units.leftText: This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that don’t go up to keep the feast of booths.
units.rightText: This will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

units.leftText: In that day there will be inscribed on the bells of the horses, “HOLY TO THE LORD”; and the pots in the LORD’s house will be like the bowls before the altar.
units.rightText: On that day, HOLY TO THE LORD will be inscribed on the bells of the horses, and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar.
rightNotes: 14:20 That is, the LORD

units.leftText: Yes, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the LORD of Armies; and all those who sacrifice will come and take of them, and cook in them. In that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Armies.
units.rightText: Indeed, every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts, and all who sacrifice will come and take some pots and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
rightNotes: 14:21 Or merchant
